_link.title: I can compare long-term potentiation and long-term depression, identifying one similarity and one difference

toLevel2.stem: What is one similarity between long-term potentiation and long-term depression?
toLevel2.answer: Both are long-lasting forms of synaptic plasticity
distractors: Both strengthen synaptic connections over time
Both involve the removal of synaptic connections
Both result from infrequent neural coactivation

toLevel2.stem: What is the key difference between LTP and LTD in terms of their effect on synaptic connections?
toLevel2.answer: LTP strengthens connections; LTD weakens them
distractors: LTP weakens connections; LTD strengthens them
Both LTP and LTD strengthen synaptic connections
Neither LTP nor LTD changes synaptic connections

toLevel2.stem: LTP results from which pattern of neural coactivation?
distractors: Infrequent coactivation
No coactivation at all
Random coactivation only

toLevel2.stem: Which mechanism of synaptic plasticity is associated with LTD?
distractors: Sprouting
Rerouting
Potentiation

toLevel2.stem: Which mechanism of synaptic plasticity is associated with LTP?
distractors: Pruning
Rerouting
Depression

toLevel2.stem: Both LTP and LTD are experience-dependent forms of synaptic plasticity that involve structural changes to the neural synapse.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: LTD results from frequent coactivation and strengthens synaptic connections through sprouting.
distractors: True

toLevel3.stem: Why are both LTP and LTD described as 'experience-dependent'?
toLevel3.answer: Both are triggered by patterns of neural activity from experience
distractors: Both occur regardless of any experience or neural activity
Both are genetically determined and fixed from early childhood
Both only occur during sleep when experiences are not present

toLevel3.stem: How does the frequency of coactivation determine whether LTP or LTD occurs?
toLevel3.answer: Frequent use leads to LTP; infrequent use leads to LTD
distractors: Frequent use leads to LTD; infrequent use leads to LTP
Frequency has no influence on which process takes place
Both processes always occur simultaneously regardless of use

toLevel3.stem: Why is it important to use the terms 'strengthening' and 'weakening' rather than informal language when comparing LTP and LTD?
toLevel3.answer: These are the precise terms expected in VCE exam responses
distractors: Informal language is always more accurate than formal terms
There is no difference between formal and informal terminology
Examiners do not assess the specific language used in answers

toLevel3.stem: Why does LTP involve sprouting while LTD involves pruning?
toLevel3.answer: Sprouting adds connections; pruning removes unused ones
distractors: Sprouting removes connections; pruning adds new growth
Both processes involve the same mechanism of change
Sprouting and pruning are interchangeable terms here

toLevel3.stem: What makes LTP and LTD similar despite having opposite effects on synaptic connections?
toLevel3.answer: Both involve lasting structural changes at the synapse
distractors: Both always strengthen the same synaptic connections
Both are temporary changes that reverse automatically
Both are caused by identical patterns of neural activity

toLevel3.stem: How do LTP and LTD work together to support effective learning?
toLevel3.answer: LTP strengthens useful pathways; LTD weakens unused ones
distractors: Both processes strengthen all pathways equally at all times
LTP and LTD cancel each other out and have no overall effect
LTD prevents LTP from occurring in any neural pathway at all

toLevel3.stem: LTP and LTD work together to support learning because LTP strengthens frequently used pathways while LTD weakens those that are no longer used.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: LTP involves {{blank:1}} because connections grow, while LTD involves {{blank:2}} because unused connections are removed.

distractors: pruning
rerouting
sprouting
rerouting

toLevel3.stem: Both LTP and LTD are similar because they both involve {{blank:1}} changes to synaptic connections in response to experience.

distractors: temporary
electrical

toLevel3.stem: Using the terms {{blank:1}} for LTP and {{blank:2}} for LTD is essential for earning full marks in VCE exam responses.

distractors: weakening
removing
strengthening
maintaining

toLevel4.stem: A musician practises guitar daily for a year. Which process describes the change in her relevant neural pathways?
distractors: LTD weakens connections through pruning
LTP weakens connections through pruning
LTD strengthens connections through sprouting

toLevel4.stem: The same musician then stops practising for a year and finds her skills have declined. Which process best explains this decline?
toLevel4.answer: LTD weakened the connections through pruning
distractors: LTP further strengthened the connections
LTD strengthened the connections even more
LTP weakened connections through sprouting

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam asks students to identify one similarity between LTP and LTD. Which response would receive full marks?
toLevel4.answer: Both are long-lasting forms of synaptic plasticity
distractors: Both strengthen synaptic connections over time
Both involve sprouting as the primary mechanism
Both result from frequent neural coactivation

toLevel4.stem: Oliver learned Spanish as a child but has not spoken it for 15 years. He now struggles to recall vocabulary. Which comparison of LTP and LTD best explains this situation?
toLevel4.answer: LTP originally strengthened the pathways; LTD has since weakened them
distractors: LTD originally strengthened the pathways; LTP has since weakened them
Both LTP and LTD worked together to maintain his Spanish vocabulary
Neither LTP nor LTD is relevant to language learning or memory loss

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'LTP makes connections bigger and LTD makes them smaller.' How should this be corrected using precise terminology?
toLevel4.answer: LTP strengthens connections; LTD weakens connections
distractors: The student's answer is already precise enough for full marks
LTP removes connections; LTD creates new connections instead
LTP weakens connections; LTD strengthens connections instead

toLevel4.stem: Priya resumes piano practice after a two-year break and gradually regains her skill. Which sequence of LTP and LTD best describes what happened across the full timeline?
toLevel4.answer: LTP during initial learning, LTD during the break, LTP during resumed practice
distractors: LTD during initial learning, LTP during the break, LTD during resumed practice
LTP throughout the entire timeline with no involvement of LTD at any point
LTD throughout the entire timeline with no involvement of LTP at any point

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam question asks for one difference between LTP and LTD. Which response would receive full marks?
toLevel4.answer: LTP strengthens connections via sprouting; LTD weakens them via pruning
distractors: LTP is temporary while LTD produces long-lasting structural changes
LTP involves structural change but LTD is only a chemical process
LTP and LTD both strengthen connections but at different intensities

toLevel4.stem: When a musician practises daily, {{blank:1}} strengthens connections via sprouting. When she stops, {{blank:2}} weakens those connections via pruning.

distractors: LTD
rerouting
LTP
sprouting

toLevel4.stem: Oliver's inability to recall Spanish vocabulary after 15 years without practice is best explained by {{blank:1}}, which {{blank:2}} the relevant synaptic connections.

distractors: LTP
sprouting
strengthened
maintained

toLevel4.stem: Using the word 'bigger' instead of '{{blank:1}}' for LTP, and 'smaller' instead of '{{blank:2}}' for LTD, would lose marks in a VCE exam.

distractors: weakening
expanding
strengthening
shrinking

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that LTD is harmful because it causes forgetting. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTD serves a useful role by removing unused connections
distractors: Correct; LTD is a pathological process that should be prevented
Correct; all weakening of connections is harmful to brain function
Incorrect; LTD does not weaken any connections in the brain at all

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee claims that LTP and LTD are completely independent processes that never interact. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; they work together to refine neural pathways for learning
distractors: Correct; LTP and LTD affect entirely separate brain areas always
Correct; the two processes have no functional connection at all
Incorrect; LTP and LTD are actually the same process by two names

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that the only difference between LTP and LTD is that one is 'good' and one is 'bad.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; both serve essential functions for effective learning
distractors: Correct; LTP is beneficial and LTD is always a negative process
Correct; value judgements are appropriate for comparing the two
Incorrect; both processes are equally harmful to all brain function

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that LTP is more important than LTD because learning is more valuable than forgetting. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Both are essential; LTD removes clutter so relevant pathways function efficiently
distractors: Correct; LTP is the only process that contributes to effective neural function
Correct; LTD contributes nothing useful and the brain would be better without it
Incorrect; LTD is more important than LTP because forgetting prevents overload

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that LTP and LTD have nothing in common because one strengthens and one weakens. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; both are long-lasting, experience-dependent forms of plasticity
distractors: Correct; having opposite effects means they share no common features
Correct; LTP involves structural change but LTD is purely a chemical change
Incorrect; LTP and LTD actually produce the same effect on all connections

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that LTD can be reversed if a person resumes practising the forgotten skill. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Supported; resumed practice can trigger LTP to restrengthen weakened connections
distractors: Unsupported; once LTD occurs, the connections are permanently destroyed
Unsupported; LTP cannot occur in pathways that were previously weakened
Supported; but only if the person practises within the first week of decline

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that both LTP and LTD involve sprouting. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTP involves sprouting but LTD involves pruning
distractors: Correct; both processes use sprouting as their mechanism of change
Correct; sprouting is the only mechanism of synaptic plasticity
Incorrect; neither LTP nor LTD involves sprouting as a mechanism

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that LTP could prevent LTD from ever occurring in the same pathway. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; a pathway strengthened by LTP can later be weakened by LTD
distractors: Correct; once LTP occurs, the pathway is permanently protected from LTD
Correct; LTP creates irreversible structural changes that prevent weakening
Incorrect; LTD always occurs before LTP and never after it in any pathway
